why: New 3D Terrain map style for Ride Mode and Map Mode (Chris asked for an onX-style 3D topo view, without copying onX): Mapbox satellite on raised ground with contour lines and peak heights in feet, plus 3D Terrain in Offline Maps downloads. Publishes with the 2.1 update.
Map Mode's Explore panel had empty space next to speed and elevation (Chris). It now also shows Heading, Trip miles and Moving time; press and hold Trip to reset it. Comes with the 2.0 update.

Checked against the Map Mode dash change: Full Map's slim bar still keeps speed, Follow Me works the same (Android now opens Map Mode zoomed in on you, as iPhone already did), and the website showcase only gained the new readings in Map Mode's text and screenshot. No change to these articles.

Fixed before release: signing out no longer shows the Before You Ride screen again on a device where someone already agreed (Chris: once when the app is downloaded unless it changes). The article now says so.
Checked against the Waypoints screen without its counts: Search and the tablet side panel work the same, so these articles are unchanged.

2.0 drops the big waypoint counts (Stops, Shared, Only You) from the Waypoints panel and the waypoint number from its Full Map bar; Chris found them confusing. Full Map's table now says the Waypoints bar shows just the map. Planned stops keep their numbers, since those give the order the group stops in.

2.0: the app now links straight to these guides. You > Help has a new first row, Help Center: How-To Guides, and the Help and Support page opens with a Help Center card and a Read the Guide link under each answer. The guides open in an in-app browser on iPhone, iPad and Android, and in the same tab on the website.
The You tab's Help menu gained a Help Center link. Nothing these guides describe changed, so only the updated date moved.

In 2.0 the Create a Ride card is now dark like Find a Ride (red flag icon instead of a red background), and both cards fill and line up evenly. The guide now names the card by its look. Events now sits right under Join, Create and Find, above Map Mode (Chris asked to move it up). Other guides that describe the home screen were checked; only the tablet guide's list changed.
Fixed the Events database update so it installs on the live server (it called a random-code function by the wrong name). Events work the same; nothing riders see changed.

Chris supplied the product photo for the Starlink Mini Mount V2 ad; the app now always shows it, so only the price comes from the store. The ad's description now says it installs on a Milwaukee Packout and also works with magnets (Chris's wording). The ad shows $249 when the store can't be reached. Gear From RUS Offroad works the same (rus-match.ts only gained the ad's fixed details).
The website showcase's Map Mode picture now says Map Mode in its description (it said Navigate). Nothing riders do on the website changed.

Chris named the next release 2.0 instead of 1.0.4. Guides written for it now say 2.0 and publish when the stores release 2.0. Battery Saver and Fix Common Problems cite lib/location.ts, where only a code comment changed; riders see no difference.
Version bump to 1.0.4 (iOS build 8, Android versionCode 8). These guides cite app/app.json; nothing riders do changed, so the text stays. 1.0.4's new guides publish once the stores release it.
Chris asked for an ad for the RUS Starlink Mini Mount V2 (Morelock Series) on the Starlink page. The Starlink guide says where it shows and what Shop the Mount does, in a 2.0 release block.

Checked after the Starlink mount ad added an Admin switch (app-settings.ts) and product-lookup helpers (rus-match.ts, lib/rus.ts). Getting started and Gear From RUS Offroad work the same for riders, so no text changed.

Server-cost work, no rider-visible change: Ride Mode now listens only to its own riders' live positions, and the ride track uploads every 2 minutes instead of on every fix (the live dot still updates on every fix; stopping sharing sends the rest). Articles checked against the code; nothing they say changed.
Create an Event (Pro since the Events change) now carries the gold Pro tag on Free too; Events and Free and Pro say so.

Free riders now see a small gold Pro tag on every button that needs Pro (Chris: show a little Pro mark next to Pro features to encourage upgrading). The article lists where the tags appear, says tapping one opens the same Pro prompt, and that Pro Trial and Pro accounts never see them. Written in a 2.0 release block.
Each Pro feature's article now says the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold Pro tag on the Free plan and none during the Pro Trial or on Pro. Written in 2.0 release blocks.

Checked after the Pro tags change touched shared screens and components (Button, groups, route builder, trips, offline map buttons, entitlements, showcase). The only change riders see is the Pro tag, covered in Free and Pro and each Pro feature's article; these articles need no text change, so only their review dates moved. Home's gold now reads the shared Colors.gold (same colour), so Your Home Screen looks the same.

Chris asked for an Events area on the home screen where Pro riders post events with photos, details, dates and a place, an agenda (concerts, raffles, poker runs) and several group rides with other riders assigned to manage them. New Events article; the Events card on the home screen, Create Events in Free and Pro, and Report an Event, all for 2.0.

Events (2.0) touched shared files these articles list (the ride page gained a Part of [event] link, the Pro list gained Create Events, Create a Ride can link to an event). Nothing these articles describe changed for riders; dates bumped after checking.

Reviewed for the Social change. Shared code they list changed (Pro comparison rows and the new social_posts feature, the Likes and Comments notification setting, profile pictures that open full size in rider lists, chats, Friends and Out Riding, new Social routes, the Friends & Social toolkit tile). Their steps read the same; the new behavior is described in Social, Free vs Pro, Notification Settings, Profile Picture, Home Screen and Friends (2.0 blocks).

Chris asked for likes, comments and interaction on every feed item, a Social area with friends, activity and comments, posts on your profile, big profile pictures with small files, sharing to Facebook, Instagram and X, a PRO tag, and comment/post/share for Pro only. New Social article; Feed, Free vs Pro, Likes and Comments notifications, reporting posts and comments, privacy of posts and photos, and full-size profile pictures added in 2.0 release blocks. The unreleased Instagram rule now only flags Instagram sign-in, since sharing to Instagram is real.

Chris asked for a place to report a rider for abuse or harassment, with an email to the admin, timed suspensions or bans, and the admin able to read the conversation. Added You > Report a Rider, the Threats reason, what happens after a report (messages saved for the OnMyLead team only, 1 to 90 day suspensions or a ban), the suspended sign-in message, and a Reports section in Privacy. Written in 2.0 release blocks.

Checked after the abuse report change touched shared files (the You tab menu, the ride page, Going list, chats, direct messages, Out Riding, sign-in, report reasons in core/pro.ts and the app layout). Only reporting changed for riders, which is in Report or Block a Rider and Privacy; these articles' steps are the same, so no text changed.

2.0 redesigns Ride Mode and the map panels: a back button and sharing line under the ride name, glass panels, three quick replies plus More (a Tell the Group sheet with every status), Regroup Here beside EMERGENCY, amber-edged announcement and regroup banners, Map Style pictures for Satellite and Topo, and riders that glide instead of jumping. New text is in 2.0 release blocks; the old steps stay until 2.0 is live.

Checked against the 2.0 Ride Mode and map redesign: these screens changed color and spacing only (glass panels and buttons, smoother rider dots and Follow Me), so the steps and labels in these articles are unchanged. The onmylead.com home page gained one sentence about the smoother Ride Mode; nothing in the website or getting-started steps changed.

Coming in 2.0: the redesigned home screen. Join a Ride first with the code box, Create a Ride with rides left this month, Find a Ride, the Map Mode card, Your Group, Public Rides Near You with a distance you pick, a Feed you can customize (whose posts, which kinds, who sees yours), badges, a toolkit and Help & Support.

Coming in 2.0: these articles point to the new home screen (Join card with Join button, rides-left label on Create, Public Rides Near You and its distance, Plan a Group Ride from the group card, the two-column tablet layout, and who sees your Feed). Old steps stay in until-2.0 blocks.

Coming in 2.0: Navigate is renamed Map Mode. Measure becomes Draw with Map a Custom Trail and a How Custom Trails Work sheet (the take-down rule from the Admin Dashboard), Track Line draws where you've been in a colour per day, Mark a Spot names obstacles on drawn and recorded trails, and shared trails now show in full with an optional Hide My Start on recordings.

Checked after the 2.0 home screen change: their code changed only in code comments (Navigation Mode renamed Map Mode), the shared bottom sheet, the You tab's Map Mode label, or a Track Line hook in the location code that riders don't see unless they turn Track Line on. The steps in these articles are unchanged.

Coming in 2.0: every rider agrees to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement on a Before You Ride screen at first launch (and on onmylead.com after signing in), and again when it changes. New article explains what it says, how to agree, where to read it again (You tab > Safety Agreement, onmylead.com/rider-agreement) and the permanent record that's saved; the related guides point to it. Written in 2.0 release blocks.

Checked after the rider agreement change touched the You tab (a Safety Agreement link next to Terms and Privacy), the app's root layout, the website footer (a Rider Safety Agreement link) and the admin rider page. Nothing these guides describe changed for riders; the agreement itself is in its own article.

Fixed: a 4 mile test ride showed about 60 miles on the ride summary. Distance now leaves out rough locations, GPS bounces, jumps while the phone says it is standing still, and gaps with location off, and points from an earlier ride no longer join the next one. The articles say what counts; written in 1.0.4 release blocks.

Checked after the ride miles fix changed how lib/location.ts saves the ride track (per ride, with each fix's accuracy, skipping fixes rougher than 100 m). Sharing, Ride Mode and Battery Saver work the same for riders, so no text changed; what counts toward distance is in Ride Summary and Ride Again.

Coming in 1.0.4: a Music button in Ride Mode and Navigate (and the Full Map bar) to play, pause, skip and change the volume of the music on the phone. Android controls any music app; iPhone and iPad control Apple Music, plus volume for any app, because Apple allows no more. Riders can hide it. New article plus 1.0.4 release blocks in the related articles.
The You tab's On the Trail section gets a Music Controls switch in 1.0.4, which shows or hides the new Music button.

Checked against the Music Controls change: it adds a Music button to Ride Mode and Navigate, a Music Controls switch to the You tab, an Apple Music permission text and a Spotify link check in the app config, a website feature card, a Music Controls flag on the Admin Settings page, and store privacy notes. Nothing these articles describe changed, so only their review dates move.

Coming in 1.0.4: Follow Me keeps the map in Ride Mode and Navigate moving with the rider (drag pauses it, Paused or Center on Me resumes, Following turns it off, remembered and also in the You tab), and the rider's own dot gets the same heading arrow as everyone else's (iPhone, iPad and Android draw their own dot with no direction). New Follow Me article; Ride Mode, Navigate, Full Map and Getting Started updated in 1.0.4 release blocks.

Reviewed for Follow Me: the You tab gains a Follow Me on Maps switch and Ride Mode gains the Follow Me button and your own heading arrow; nothing these articles describe changed (the showcase text now mentions Follow Me).

Coming in 1.0.4: the app checks the App Store or Google Play itself and shows Update Available on the home screen when a newer version is out, so the FAQ explains how riders find out about a new version. Written in a 1.0.4 release block.
Full Map's Ride Mode bar keeps the rider line, which on a Freeride (new in 1.0.4) shows the group behind the leader.

Coming in 1.0.4: on a Freeride (no mapped route), Ride Mode's line shows every sharing rider in order behind the leader, measured along the path the leader has ridden (kept on each phone, never uploaded), with the group's spread and how far the leader is ahead. Written in a 1.0.4 release block so it shows once 1.0.4 is out.

Coming in 1.0.4: says that on a Freeride each rider's phone keeps the leader's path (from the live location riders already see) to measure the group's spread, that it stays on the phone, and that it is cleared after 18 hours or on the next Freeride.
Ride Mode's screen code changed to show the rider line on Freeride rides (see Use Ride Mode). These guides list Ride Mode as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.
Coming in 1.0.4: Full Map on every map (Ride Mode, Navigate, Draw a Route, Waypoints, Find a Ride). Chris asked for as much map as possible in every mode, with the buttons easy to bring back.

Coming in 1.0.4: where Full Map is on each map and what stays on screen. Ride Mode's Menus button is now Controls (same name on every map), the bar also swipes up, Center on Me and No Signal stay, and the phone remembers Full Map.

Checked against the Full Map change, which touched screens these guides describe (Ride Mode, the route builder, waypoints, Find a Ride, the map layers button). Nothing they say changed; Full Map has its own guide.

Coming in 1.0.4: Ride Mode has a ✎ Message button to type a short message of your own to the group (sent like a quick reply, with Seen by and Cancel) and to keep up to 6 of your own quick replies on the device.
Checked against the Ride Mode message change: only a new ✎ Message button and sheet in Ride Mode (and a line on the website's Ride Mode section) were added, so nothing in these articles changed.

Coming in 1.0.4: an easier way to leave a ride. Leave Ride moved from the bottom of the Riders section to the bottom of every ride page and into Ride Mode's Riders sheet and tablet sidebar, always confirms, and stops location sharing for the ride. Pending and waitlisted riders see Withdraw. Organizers can now leave by picking who takes the ride over (or cancel when nobody else has joined).
Coming in 1.0.4: where Leave Ride is on a tablet (bottom of the ride page's left side and of the Riders list in Ride Mode), and that an organizer can leave by handing the ride to another rider.

These guides list the ride page, Ride Mode or location sharing as a source, which the 1.0.4 Leave Ride change touched (a Leave Ride button at the bottom of the ride page and under Riders in Ride Mode). Nothing they describe changes for riders.

New in 1.0.4: a bell on the Rides tab opens Notifications, the notifications OnMyLead sent you in the last 30 days. Open one, Mark All Read, swipe one away to clear it (X on the website), or Clear All, which also clears the phone's own notification list and the app icon badge. Notification Settings links from the bottom of the list.

The Rides tab now has a notifications bell at the top right, and the app keeps its saved notifications current in the background. These guides list the Rides tab, the app's screen list or the message pop-ups as sources; nothing in them changes for riders.

New guide Make Your Location Accurate, after an Android rider beside Chris showed 1.5 miles away (Google Maps on that phone was off by the same amount; the fix was Precise Location plus Google Location Accuracy and a calibration). The phone steps are true today. For 1.0.4: Android asks for Google Location Accuracy when sharing starts, and Ride Mode's banner also covers Google Location Accuracy off and a rough fix (with calibration steps).

A rider who joined from Android showed about 1.5 miles away while sitting next to the organizer: their phone had Approximate location. Fix Common Problems now explains how to turn on Precise Location on Android, iPhone and iPad (true today). For 1.0.4: Ride Mode shows a Precise Location Is Off banner that asks for precise location (Android) or opens Settings (iPhone, iPad), the riders list labels Approximate Location, and Ride Bubble no longer calls such a rider separated for a gap their rough location could explain.

Ride Mode and location sharing changed for riders on Approximate Location (a new banner and an Approximate Location label, written up in Use Ride Mode, Share Your Location and Fix Common Problems). Nothing in these guides changes; on a tablet the banner sits with the others in the sidebar.

The onmylead.com homepage now also shows the rest of 1.0.3 (heading arrows, Center on Me, trails from farther out, sharing until you turn it off, swipe-down sheets, hold-to-send Emergency, update heads-ups) and a new Ride Mode picture. These guides list the homepage as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.

New in 1.0.3: Profile Pictures. Riders can take a photo or choose one from their library (cropped square and shrunk to 512 pixels), change it or remove it from Your Name and Picture. It shows in place of their initial in ride rider lists, riding groups, ride and group chat, Messages, Friends, Out Riding and the You tab, to signed-in riders only like the ride name. Report a rider now has Inappropriate Photo, and the OnMyLead team can remove a picture.

Reviewed for profile pictures (1.0.3). These articles share code that changed: rider dots in lists and chat now show a rider's picture when they have one, the report sheet gained Inappropriate Photo, the You tab name row says Your name and picture, and the camera permission is now asked for profile pictures. The steps in these articles are unchanged; the new behavior is described in Add a Profile Picture.

Fix before 1.0.3 ships: the friend code (and, on long codes, the ride invite code) showed tiny on iPhone after custom codes arrived. Codes now show at full size again. Nothing in these articles changes for riders.

New in 1.0.3: Choose Your Own Code. Organizers can type their own ride invite code (when creating the ride or later from the invite card), group owners their group code, and every rider their friend link code, like MOAB-2026. The app checks live that no one else uses it; the old link stops working when a code changes.

These articles list ride page, ride creation or app files that changed for custom share codes (the invite card's Choose Your Own Code, long codes shrinking to fit). Nothing in them changes for riders.
1.0.3 moves to iPhone and iPad build 7 and Android versionCode 7 (build 6 was uploaded but not submitted). These articles list the app config as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.

Navigate's map now follows you while you record a trail or follow one you're near, and after you tap Center on Me (the button turns white while following). Dragging or pinching the map pauses following until you tap Center on Me again. Found while testing 1.0.3 on Android, where the dot could leave the screen while recording.

New in 1.0.3: Friends. Add riders you've ridden with, riders you see Out Riding or message with, or anyone with your friend link (no search by name). Friends see each other in Out Riding and can message any time. Blocking ends a friendship. Adds a Friend Requests notification switch, and Add Friend and Message on a ride's Going list.

Friends touched shared files these articles list (the ride's Going list, notification topics, the app layout, app links in app.json and ride-link.ts, and the website showcase). Nothing they describe changes for riders, apart from the new Add Friend and Message buttons on the Going list, which Add Friends covers.

Mappers can delete their own trails: Delete Trail in My Trails (also takes a shared trail, its photos and ratings off the public map) and Delete Your Trail on a shared trail's page. Past rides keep their route.

Recording trails, sharing trails and group rides on your own trails are now Pro. The Navigate map, measuring, following and rating trails stay free. Report or Block, Ride Polls and Subscribe to Pro read the same Pro list and need no wording change.

New in 1.0.3: Navigate, an offroad map for riding on your own. Record or draw trails, keep them on your phone or share them with a name, difficulty and vehicles, add photos, rate other riders' trails for quality and line accuracy (trails rated inaccurate are hidden and the mapper is told), measure distances, and use a trail as a group ride's route. Rider trails show as mint dotted lines on every map, with a switch to hide them.

Checked against the Navigation Mode change, which touches shared screens (Home, the You tab, the ride form, the route builder and the maps). Nothing these articles describe looks or works differently.
Ride Mode's map now opens centered on the rider at riding zoom (it could open over a random spot or the whole world), and Center on Me zooms in when the map is zoomed far out. Ships in 1.0.3.

Ride Mode's map now opens centered on the rider (see Use Ride Mode). These articles list Ride Mode as a source; nothing in them changes for riders. The live.webp screenshot still matches: only where the map starts changed.

New in 1.0.3: Out Riding. Switch it on to see which riders are out near you (riders you know by default, or everyone nearby who chose the same), roughly how far away in whole miles, never where, and message them. Adds direct messages with mute, report, block and delete, and a Direct Messages notification switch.
Out Riding touched shared files these articles list (the Groups tab, notification topics, the app layout, message pop-ups and the website showcase). Nothing in them changes for riders.

New in 1.0.3: riders earn Bronze, Silver and Gold badges (Trail Boss, Tail Gunner, Crew Rider, Mile Eater, Trailblazer, Mapmaker, Trail Scout) and a rank from Rookie to Legend, shown on the You tab, on a new Badges screen and beside rider names. The account notification switch is now Badges and Pro Trial, and a badge notification opens Badges.

The badges change touched screens these articles list as sources (the You tab, the Going list, the Riders list, notification settings and the app's screen list, and the onmylead.com features list, which gains a Badges and Ranks card). Nothing these articles describe changes for riders.

App version goes to 1.0.3 (iPhone and iPad build 6, Android versionCode 6). 1.0.2 was never released, so 1.0.3 carries its changes too. These articles list the app config as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.

Ride Mode's route line now shows every sharing rider's dot in running order without dots hiding each other (tap one for the rider's name and place), and a new Full Map view hides everything but that line, EMERGENCY and a Menus button. Ships in 1.0.3.

These guides list Ride Mode, the route strip or the website home page as a source. Ride Mode gains the rider order line and Full Map (covered in Use Ride Mode); the website's Ride Together step mentions them. Nothing these guides describe changes.
1.0.3 adds Update Required, Update Available and About This Version notices that the owner sets from the new Admin Releases page; the FAQ explains what riders see and that Not Now always works.

These guides list the home screen notices, app settings or the root layout as sources. The change adds release controls (Update Required, Update Available, About This Version), covered in the FAQ; the feature switches, notices and screens these guides describe work as before.

Version 1.0.3 fixes rider dots in Ride Mode drifting off the rider's real position as the map zooms, and restyles them: a white ring for each rider and a bigger solid blue dot for the leader, with dark name tags. The new look is described in 1.0.3 release blocks. Moving riders' dots also get a heading arrow (from the GPS course they already share), described in the same 1.0.3 block.

These guides list map pin or website files as sources. Their pins (waypoints, planned stops, search results, Find ride pins) are now placed exactly on their spot, and the website's sample rider dots match the new look; nothing they describe changes. Ride Mode's screen file also changed only to pass each rider's heading to the map, so the Ride Mode guides that list it describe nothing new.

Chris tapped EMERGENCY in Ride Mode and nothing seemed to happen: Alert My Group needed a 1.5 second hold with no sign it was working, and the screen stayed up while the alert sent. From 1.0.3 the button fills a bar and says Keep Holding, a quick tap says Not sent, and the screen closes as soon as the alert goes out.
These guides list the Ride Mode screen as a source. Only the Emergency sheet's Alert My Group button changes (covered in Emergencies and Staying Safe); nothing they describe changes.

Every sheet that slides up (a new or open waypoint, Riders, Directions, Share Your Location, Emergency, a report, the Pro prompt and the ride QR code) now closes when you swipe it down, on iPhone, iPad and Android. A rider couldn't swipe away the New Waypoint sheet and had to tap Cancel. In the app from 1.0.3.

These guides list Ride Mode, Directions, the Pro prompt or the QR code as a source. Only the way their sheets close changed (swipe down, covered in Use Ride Mode and Getting Started); nothing these guides describe changes.

These guides list Create a Ride or the website home page as a source. Only the time fields changed (now tap-to-pick, covered in Create a Ride) and one line of showcase copy; nothing these guides describe changes.

Times are now picked by tapping AM or PM, the hour and the minute instead of typing "8:00 am": Meet At, Departure Time, Expected Finish, Stop Sharing At and a planned stop's time. In the app from 1.0.3; on the website from its next deploy.

App version goes to 1.0.2 (iPhone and iPad build 5, Android versionCode 5) for the store update with the trails, Center on Me, 2027 dates and calendar, share until turned off and iOS contact page fixes. These articles list the app config as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.
These guides list the website home page as a source. Its footer only gains a Release Notes link; nothing they describe changes.

Chris asked for a page on the website with the changelog and release notes for every app version. onmylead.com/help/release-notes is built from help/release-notes.json and shows each version once the App Store or Google Play has it (1.0 and 1.0.1 today; 1.0.2 is written and appears when a store releases it). It is linked from the Help Center menu, home page and footer and the website footer. The FAQ gets a question pointing to it.

Chris found that Ride Mode only showed roads and trails when zoomed way in, and that they flashed when zooming out. OpenStreetMap tracks now show from about 15 miles across (the same zoom on iPad and Android tablets as on a phone), the longest trails are drawn first when zoomed far out, and lines on screen stay put while the map moves. The app text ships with 1.0.2; the website change goes live with the next website deploy. Offline Maps only lists these files as sources: downloads save the same squares as before, so nothing changes there for riders.

Chris asked for a way to share location forever, until the rider turns it off, plus a calendar to pick when sharing ends. From 1.0.2, Until I Turn It Off has no 24-hour cap on personal shares, ride shares get the same option (still ending with the ride), both share screens get Pick an End Date (a calendar plus a time, up to a year out), the You tab shows an active personal share, and the family link page says When they turn it off. Old text stays for 1.0 and 1.0.1 in until blocks.

These guides list Ride Mode's screen or the You tab as a source. The change there is the location sharing sheet (Until I Turn It Off, Pick an End Date) and the Share My Location row on the You tab saying when an active share ends; both are covered in Share Your Location. Nothing these guides describe changes.

Create a Ride: rides can now be set up to three years out (2027 and later work), and the calendar lets riders type a date or jump to any month and year. App text is in a 1.0.2 block; the website gets it on its next deploy.
These articles list the Create a Ride screen as a source. Only its ride-day picker and the out-of-range message changed; nothing in these articles changes for riders.

iPhone and iPad: opening Help and Support, Contact Us, Terms or Privacy no longer shows an 'Expo Head: Add the handoff origin' alert. Page titles are now set only on the website. No article text changes; the pages work the same.

Ride Mode gets a Center on Me button (iPhone, iPad, Android phones and tablets) that moves the map to your location in the open part of the map, keeping the zoom. Ships with 1.0.2, so the text is in a release block.

These guides list Ride Mode's screen as a source. Adding the Center on Me button changes nothing they describe; the button is covered in Use Ride Mode. The live.webp screenshot is unchanged because the website's Ride Mode has no live map and no button.
Apple released OnMyLead 1.0 in the US App Store on 2026-10-28. release.json now marks 1.0 live, so the guides drop the 'waiting for review' notice.
App version goes to 1.0.1 (iPhone and iPad build 4, Android versionCode 4) to match the 1.0.1 beta builds. These articles list the app config as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.

Chris asked for trails that are easier to see, trail and road names on the maps, and closed trails made visible on every device and the website. Trail lines are bolder, OpenStreetMap trails get name tags, Forest Service lines show names and numbers, and closed roads and trails (Forest Service, BLM, OpenStreetMap, plus today's seasonal closures) are red with a Closed note on the trail card. The app part ships in 1.0.1; the website gets the layers panel, topo and these layers at its next deploy. The route builder and offline maps guides mention the website layers and saved closed roads; the other guides only had their date bumped (their maps share the trail layer, nothing else changed for them).

On onmylead.com the Rides list relied on swiping, which doesn't work with a mouse. Each ride row on the website now has a Delete, Leave or Decline button, and the article says where it is. Articles that describe the Rides tab were checked; on phones and tablets nothing changed.

Chris couldn't find a way to search for a location while building a ride on the website. The waypoints map now has the same Search as the route builder (parks, trailheads, towns, addresses), and the website guide points to the search boxes. The route builder's first hint now mentions Search; the other guides only had their date bumped (no visible change for them).
1.0.1 adds Report a Bug on the You tab: a screenshot, the phone model and app version, and a short app activity log go with the message so problems testers find can be fixed fast.
Reviewed for Report a Bug, which logs failed requests from the shared server connection. Nothing riders do in these articles changes.

New in 1.0.1: Battery Saver lets riders choose how often their phone sends its location while sharing (Best Accuracy, Balanced, Max Battery Saver), starting on Best Accuracy and warning before switching away from it. Share Your Location, Ride Mode and Troubleshooting point to it in 1.0.1 blocks.
Reviewed for Battery Saver (new You tab row, a Change link on Share My Location, and Ride Mode's sharing banner naming the setting). The steps in these articles don't change.

Create a Ride's day used to be limited to the next two weeks. 1.0.1 and the website add a Calendar button to pick any day from today up to a year out, plus Sat and Sun quick picks for the coming weekend.
Reviewed for the Create a Ride calendar. The steps in these articles don't change; Ride Again still sets the next day on the same weekday.

Bug fix for 1.0.1: if you turned off location for OnMyLead mid-share, Ride Mode kept saying you were sharing while nothing was sent. It now shows a one-time Location Is Off notice, and the article says so.
Reviewed for the Location Is Off fix in Ride Mode. The steps in these articles don't change.

Bug fix: signing out on one device (for example an iPad) also signed you out on your other devices, so your phone showed "Please sign in first." and stopped sharing your location. Sign Out now affects only the device you tap it on, and the article says so.
Reviewed for the sign-out fix: Home now clears an old error message when you sign in to a different account. The steps in these articles don't change.

OnMyLead 1.0 build 3 goes to the App Store for iPhone and iPad and to Google Play for Android phones and tablets, so iPad and Android are no longer unreleased. The Android and tablet steps that were held back now show, the tablet guide is published, "iPhone only" and "no iPad version" wording is gone, ride pages offer Google Play on Android, and the notification-tap steps written for 1.1.0 show now because build 3 carries them.
Android build number goes to 3 for the next Google Play upload. These articles list the app config as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.

Bug fix: after signing out, or signing in to another account, Home, Groups and the You tab kept showing the previous account's rides, groups and ride name until they reloaded. They now clear as soon as the account changes. The steps in these articles don't change, so only their dates were bumped.

Bug fix: tapping an emailed sign-in link while the sign-in screen was still open showed Home inside that screen (a floating card on iPad). The app now closes the sign-in screen first, so the link opens Home normally. The article says the link opens Home.

On Android, sign-in, confirm-email and password-reset links used to sign in the browser instead of the app. The website now hands them to the Android app. The article says so in an Android-only block, hidden until the Android app is released. Troubleshooting lists the sign-in link code as a source; nothing in it changes for riders.

Bug fix: on Android, Ride Mode with location sharing on asked for location permission over and over and could bounce the app to the home screen. The app now asks only when access isn't given yet. Riders still see the same first-time question, so no article wording changes; these articles list Ride Mode or the location code as a source.

Ride Mode now adds a rider who joins while you're on the map within a few seconds (it used to wait for the 15 second refresh), and drops riders whose share ends. The article says so. The other Ride Mode articles list the screen as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.

Bug fix: on Android, a location share resumed after an app update, force-stop or phone restart now really sends again when Ride Mode opens. Ride Mode's Android note now says so; the other articles already describe it (app.json only bumps the Android build number).
Android now shows the whole logo on the launch screen and keeps the app icon inside every launcher shape. These articles list the app config as a source; nothing in them changes for riders.

With one rider, or the whole group at the meeting spot, the Ride Mode map now frames about a mile around them instead of zooming past where map tiles exist (it showed blank or blurry). Nothing the articles describe changes, so only the dates moved.

Back from a screen opened by a notification now returns to Home instead of leaving the app (issue #109). Ride Mode says so from 1.1.0; Promo Codes lists the app's root layout as a source, and nothing about it changes for riders.

Tapping a notification now always opens the ride, chat or group it is about, including when the tap starts the app. Android was opening Home instead. Notification Settings now says where each kind of notification takes you (from version 1.1.0); Get Started mentions it too.

The Privacy Policy now names Google as a service for Android (Firebase notifications, Google Play purchases, Google Maps). The guide says Apple is used on iPhone; the Android line stays hidden until the Android app is on Google Play.

Tablet layouts for iPad and Android tablets: the map fills the screen with the riders and buttons beside it in Ride Mode, the ride page shows details beside the map, riders and chat, and the tabs run down the left. The tablet steps sit in tablet release blocks and the new tablet guide is a draft, so nothing tablet-only shows until a tablet build is in a store. Find a Ride and Getting Started now say how the website looks on a computer (list beside the map, tabs down the left), which goes live with the next website deploy. Every other listed guide only gained the search word "tablet": phones look exactly as before.

Groundwork for Pro on Android: subscribing, cancelling, restoring and promo codes through Google Play, and one Pro for every device whichever store it came from (the other store's Pro screen won't sell it twice). The Android steps sit in Android release blocks, so nothing shows on the website until the Android app is on Google Play. The safety guide now says plainly that nothing on it needs Pro. Nothing changes for iPhone riders.

Groundwork for the Android app: Android steps for location (While Using the App plus the Sharing Your Location notification), notification categories, Google Maps directions, photos and invite links. They sit in Android release blocks, so nothing shows on the website until the Android app is on Google Play. The offline maps guide now says "the live satellite view" instead of naming Apple, matching the app. Nothing else changes for iPhone riders.
The website's top bar now shows Help on phones and tablets too, so the guides say where to find it.

Fixed two bugs: on I Approve Riders rides, the ride's link or invite code let riders skip approval, and Approve could put a ride over Max Riders or Max Vehicles. The guide is published again and says what now happens.
First version of the Help Center, written from the app's code at the 1.0 App Store build (ad388f4).
